concepts.explanation: Examples include carbon and aluminium (metal extraction by reducing metal oxides), SO2 (preservative/bleaching), and vitamin C (reduces Fe3+ to Fe2+ to aid absorption). Reducing agents are oxidised.

concepts.name: Permanganate reduction half‑equation in acidic solution
concepts.explanation: In acidic medium, permanganate is reduced from Mn(+7) to Mn(+2): MnO4− + 8H+ + 5e− → Mn2+ + 4H2O. This half‑reaction underpins many redox titrations.

concepts.name: Acidification with sulfuric acid in permanganate titrations
concepts.explanation: Dilute H2SO4 supplies H+ to drive MnO4− reduction to Mn2+. HCl is avoided (Cl− oxidized to Cl2) and HNO3 avoided (oxidizing agent). Insufficient acid gives MnO2 precipitate.

concepts.name: MnO4−/Fe2+ titration stoichiometry (1:5)
concepts.explanation: In acidic solution, 1 mol permanganate oxidizes 5 mol iron(II): MnO4− + 8H+ + 5Fe2+ → Mn2+ + 5Fe3+ + 4H2O. The 1:5 ratio is essential for calculations.

concepts.name: Potassium permanganate as a self‑indicator (faint permanent pink endpoint)
concepts.explanation: KMnO4 solutions are intensely purple and decolorize upon reduction. In titrations, the first faint permanent pink indicates excess MnO4− and marks the endpoint.

concepts.name: Potassium permanganate is not a primary standard
concepts.explanation: KMnO4 cannot be weighed for a standard solution due to limited purity and instability (decomposes with light/heat); its solutions drift in concentration over time.

concepts.name: Standardization of KMnO4 with ammonium iron(II) sulfate (Mohr’s salt)
concepts.explanation: A primary standard solution of ammonium iron(II) sulfate is titrated with KMnO4 in acid to determine the exact permanganate concentration.

concepts.name: Ammonium iron(II) sulfate (Mohr’s salt) as a primary standard
concepts.explanation: Mohr’s salt, (NH4)2SO4·FeSO4·6H2O, is stable, high molar mass, and not air‑oxidized; dissolved in dilute H2SO4 to stabilize Fe2+, making it suitable as a primary standard.

concepts.name: Efflorescence
concepts.explanation: Spontaneous loss of water of crystallization from hydrated salts (e.g., FeSO4·7H2O, CuSO4·5H2O), undermining mass accuracy for primary standards.

concepts.name: Hygroscopic substances
concepts.explanation: Materials that absorb moisture from air without dissolving (e.g., anhydrous FeSO4, conc. H2SO4), complicating accurate weighing for standards.

concepts.name: Deliquescence
concepts.explanation: Spontaneous absorption of moisture from air until a substance dissolves (e.g., NaOH, KOH), affecting handling and concentration control.

concepts.name: Permanganate in neutral/basic solution forms MnO2 precipitate
concepts.explanation: Without sufficient acid, MnO4− reduces to MnO2(s) (brown): MnO4− + 2H2O + 3e− → MnO2(s) + 4OH−, invalidating the titration.

concepts.name: Stoichiometric titration relationship V·M/n for redox reactions
concepts.explanation: The equivalence relation V_o·M_o/n_o = V_r·M_r/n_r links volumes, molarities, and stoichiometric coefficients in redox titrations.

concepts.name: Autocatalysis by Mn2+ in permanganate titrations
concepts.explanation: Mn2+ produced during reduction of permanganate catalyzes the reaction, causing decolorization to speed up as titration progresses.

concepts.name: Iodine–thiosulfate reaction stoichiometry
concepts.explanation: I2 is reduced by thiosulfate to I− while thiosulfate is oxidized to tetrathionate: I2 + 2 S2O3^2− → S4O6^2− + 2 I−. Basis of iodometric titrations.

concepts.name: Standardization of sodium thiosulfate using standard iodine
concepts.explanation: Because Na2S2O3·5H2O is not a primary standard (efflorescent, variable water), its solution is standardized by titration against a standard iodine solution.

concepts.name: Generation of iodine by acidified permanganate and excess iodide
concepts.explanation: Acidified MnO4− oxidizes I− to I2: 2MnO4− + 10I− + 16H+ → 2Mn2+ + 5I2 + 8H2O. Excess KI ensures complete reaction and maximal, measurable iodine.

concepts.name: Triiodide (I3−) formation and iodine solubility in KI
concepts.explanation: Iodine dissolves in KI solution by forming I3− (I2 + I− → I3−), a charged species that is much more soluble in water, facilitating iodometric titrations.

concepts.name: Starch indicator in iodometry (add near endpoint)
concepts.explanation: Starch forms a blue‑black complex with iodine; added when the solution is pale yellow to avoid iodine adsorption that would slow the endpoint and reduce accuracy.

concepts.name: Chlorine interference in iodometric titrations
concepts.explanation: Dissolved chlorine oxidizes I− to I2 (Cl2 + 2I− → 2Cl− + I2), inflating iodine levels. Use distilled water to avoid chlorine contamination.

concepts.name: Determination of elemental iron in tablets by permanganate titration
concepts.explanation: Iron tablets are dissolved in dilute H2SO4 and aliquots titrated with standardized KMnO4; results convert to FeSO4 and elemental Fe per tablet.

concepts.name: Reading the top of the meniscus for dark solutions
concepts.explanation: For intensely colored solutions like KMnO4 where the lower meniscus is hard to see, burette readings are taken from the top of the meniscus for consistency.

concepts.name: Titration stoichiometry formula (V×M/n equivalence)
concepts.explanation: At equivalence, V_ox×M_ox/n_ox = V_red×M_red/n_red links volumes, molarities, and electron ratios to compute unknown concentrations in titrations.

concepts.name: Permanganate–iron(II) redox titration endpoint
concepts.explanation: KMnO4 acts as a self-indicator; the endpoint is the first faint permanent pink in an acidic Fe2+ solution, reflecting slight excess permanganate.

concepts.name: Acidic conditions for permanganate titrations
concepts.explanation: Permanganate must be titrated in strong acid (e.g., dilute H2SO4) to ensure MnO4− is reduced to Mn2+; insufficient acid leads to side products.

concepts.name: MnO2 precipitation from insufficient acid in KMnO4 titration
concepts.explanation: If the medium is not sufficiently acidic, MnO4− is reduced to brown MnO2(s), causing endpoint errors and cloudy mixtures.

concepts.name: Mohr’s salt as a primary standard
concepts.explanation: Hydrated ammonium iron(II) sulfate [(NH4)2SO4·FeSO4·6H2O] is stable, pure, non-hygroscopic, and soluble, making it suitable for standard solutions.

concepts.name: Role of sulfuric acid in Fe2+ standard solutions
concepts.explanation: Dilute H2SO4 is added when preparing Fe2+ solutions to minimize aerial oxidation of Fe2+ to Fe3+ during storage and use.

concepts.name: Iodometry: iodine–thiosulfate reaction
concepts.explanation: I2 + 2 S2O3^2− → 2 I− + S4O6^2− underpins iodometric titrations, with a 1:2 stoichiometric ratio (I2:thiosulfate).

concepts.name: Starch indicator timing and color change in iodometry
concepts.explanation: Starch is added near the endpoint (pale yellow) to avoid iodine–starch complex stability; endpoint is blue-black to colorless.

concepts.name: Triiodide formation to solubilize iodine
concepts.explanation: I2 dissolves in aqueous KI by forming I3− (I2 + I− → I3−), enabling accurate aqueous titration.

concepts.name: Preparation of a standard solution in a volumetric flask
concepts.explanation: Dissolve, transfer with rinsings, make to the mark, and mix by repeated inversion to achieve a homogeneous known-concentration solution.

concepts.name: Proper pipette technique and rinsing
concepts.explanation: Rinse with water then solution, fill to mark at eye level, drain without blowing the last drop, and touch off to ensure accurate delivery.

concepts.name: Rinsing protocols for burette, pipette, and conical flask
concepts.explanation: Rinse burette and pipette with the solutions they will contain; do not rinse the conical flask with reagent to avoid volume errors.

concepts.name: Systematic errors in titration
concepts.explanation: Consistent one-direction biases (e.g., wrong indicator, overshooting endpoint, improper rinsing) shift results and reduce accuracy.

concepts.name: Random errors in titration
concepts.explanation: Unpredictable fluctuations from trial to trial (e.g., inconsistent mixing, lighting, reaction time) affect precision and can be reduced by averaging.

concepts.name: Accuracy versus precision in volumetric analysis
concepts.explanation: Systematic errors reduce accuracy without necessarily affecting precision; random errors reduce precision but may average to accurate results.

concepts.name: Meniscus reading at eye level (parallax minimization)
concepts.explanation: Reading the meniscus at eye level prevents parallax error in volumetric measurements, improving consistency and accuracy.

concepts.name: Use of conical flask and swirling in titration
concepts.explanation: A conical flask facilitates safe swirling and efficient mixing during titration, aiding endpoint detection and reaction completion.

concepts.name: Effect of water quality on iodometric titration
concepts.explanation: Distilled water is preferred over deionised water to minimize oxidizing contaminants (e.g., residual chlorine) that can alter iodine levels.

concepts.name: Converting molarity to grams per litre for hydrated salts
concepts.explanation: Use molar mass of the hydrate (e.g., Na2S2O3·5H2O) to convert molarity to g/L for reporting concentrations of crystalline reagents.

concepts.name: Pentahydrate and water of crystallization
concepts.explanation: A pentahydrate contains five moles of water per mole of salt in its crystal lattice, affecting molar mass and solution preparation.

concepts.name: Mole calculation from mass and molar mass
concepts.explanation: n = mass/Mr enables determining moles of a solute for stoichiometric and concentration calculations.

concepts.name: Mole calculation from solution volume and molarity
concepts.explanation: n = (V_cm3 × M)/1000 converts a measured volume and molarity into moles for titration and solution stoichiometry.

concepts.name: Rate of Reaction
concepts.explanation: The change in concentration of a reactant or product per unit time; a quantitative measure of how fast a chemical change occurs.

concepts.name: Collision Theory
concepts.explanation: A model stating reactions occur when particles collide with sufficient energy and proper orientation; only effective collisions produce products.

concepts.name: Activation Energy
concepts.explanation: The minimum energy that colliding particles must possess for a collision to be effective and result in products.

concepts.name: Effect of Temperature on Reaction Rate
concepts.explanation: Increasing temperature increases particle energy and the fraction of effective collisions, often roughly doubling rate for each 10°C rise.

concepts.name: Effect of Surface Area (Particle Size) on Reaction Rate
concepts.explanation: Smaller particles provide more surface area, increasing collision opportunities and speeding heterogeneous reactions.

concepts.name: Effect of Nature of Reactants on Reaction Rate
concepts.explanation: Ionic reactions in solution are typically fast as ions are already dissociated; covalent reactions are slower due to bond breaking requirements.

concepts.name: Effect of Pressure on Gas-Phase Reaction Rate
concepts.explanation: For reactions of gases, increasing pressure compresses gases into smaller volumes, raising collision frequency and increasing rate.

concepts.name: Average Rate of Reaction
concepts.explanation: Total change in a measured quantity (e.g., concentration or volume) divided by the total time interval over which it changes.

concepts.name: Instantaneous Rate of Reaction
concepts.explanation: The reaction rate at a specific moment, obtained from the slope of the tangent to a concentration- or volume–time curve at that time.

concepts.name: Initial Rate of Reaction
concepts.explanation: The instantaneous rate at the start (t = 0), when reactant concentrations are maximal; often used to compare reaction conditions.

concepts.name: Reaction Profile Diagram (Energy Profile)
concepts.explanation: A graph of potential energy versus reaction progress showing reactants, products, activation energy, and the activated complex.

concepts.name: Exothermic vs Endothermic Energy Profiles
concepts.explanation: Exothermic profiles end at lower energy than reactants (negative ΔH); endothermic profiles end higher (positive ΔH).

concepts.name: Maxwell–Boltzmann Energy Distribution
concepts.explanation: The statistical distribution of molecular energies at a given temperature; area above Ea correlates with fraction of effective collisions.

concepts.name: Catalysts (Definition and Properties)
concepts.explanation: Substances that alter reaction rate without being consumed; often specific, effective in small amounts, and do not change equilibrium position.

concepts.name: Catalyst Lowers Activation Energy
concepts.explanation: Catalysts provide an alternative reaction pathway with lower Ea, increasing the fraction of effective collisions and the rate.

concepts.name: Homogeneous Catalysis
concepts.explanation: Catalysis where catalyst and reactants are in the same phase, with no boundary between them (e.g., I− catalysis of H2O2).

concepts.name: Heterogeneous Catalysis
concepts.explanation: Catalysis where catalyst and reactants are in different phases; involves adsorption, surface reaction, and desorption steps.

concepts.name: Autocatalysis
concepts.explanation: A reaction in which one of the products acts as a catalyst, causing the rate to increase as the reaction proceeds.

concepts.name: Intermediate Formation Theory of Catalysis
concepts.explanation: Catalysis mechanism where the catalyst forms a reactive intermediate with a reactant, which then converts to products regenerating the catalyst.

concepts.name: Surface Adsorption Theory of Catalysis
concepts.explanation: Heterogeneous catalysis mechanism involving adsorption of reactants, reaction on the surface, and desorption of products at active sites.

concepts.name: Active Sites in Heterogeneous Catalysis
concepts.explanation: Specific surface locations on a catalyst where adsorption and reaction occur; number and availability govern catalytic effectiveness.

concepts.name: Catalyst Poisoning
concepts.explanation: Deactivation of a catalyst when strongly adsorbed impurities (e.g., Pb, S, P, silicates) block active sites, reducing catalytic activity.

concepts.name: Catalytic Converter (Automotive)
concepts.explanation: An exhaust device using Pt, Pd, Rh catalysts on a honeycomb to convert CO, NOx, and hydrocarbons into CO2, N2, and H2O.

concepts.name: Enzymes as Biological Catalysts
concepts.explanation: Protein catalysts (e.g., catalase, protease) that exhibit high specificity and operate under mild conditions to accelerate reactions.

concepts.name: Gas Collection Method for Measuring Reaction Rate
concepts.explanation: Determining rate by measuring volume of gas evolved over time using collection over water or a gas syringe.

concepts.name: Mass Loss Method for Measuring Reaction Rate
concepts.explanation: Tracking rate by monitoring mass decrease when a gaseous product escapes (e.g., CO2 from CaCO3 + HCl).

concepts.name: Disappearing Cross Method (Sodium Thiosulfate Reaction)
concepts.explanation: Measuring time for sulfur precipitate to obscure a cross; rate is taken as 1/time to reach a set turbidity.

concepts.name: Tangent Method for Determining Instantaneous Rate
concepts.explanation: Finding the slope of a tangent to a volume- or concentration–time graph at a given time to obtain instantaneous rate.

concepts.name: Effective Collision
concepts.explanation: A collision with sufficient energy and proper orientation to overcome activation energy and form products.

concepts.name: Activated Complex (Transition State)
concepts.explanation: A high-energy, short-lived arrangement of atoms at the peak of the energy profile formed during an effective collision.

concepts.name: Saturation Effect in Surface Reactions
concepts.explanation: At high reactant concentration, surface sites become fully occupied, so further concentration increases do not raise the rate.

concepts.name: Dust Explosions and Reaction Rate
concepts.explanation: Finely divided combustible powders react rapidly due to large surface area; explosions require fuel dust, oxygen, dryness, ignition, and confinement.
concepts.broader_concept: Effect of Surface Area on Reaction Rate

concepts.name: Dynamic Chemical Equilibrium
concepts.explanation: A reversible reaction state where the forward and reverse reaction rates are equal, so concentrations remain constant while both reactions continue.

concepts.name: Le Chatelier's Principle
concepts.explanation: If a stress (change in concentration, pressure, or temperature) is applied to a system at equilibrium, the system shifts to counteract the stress and establish a new equilibrium.

concepts.name: Law of Chemical Equilibrium and Kc
concepts.explanation: For a balanced reaction aA + bB ⇌ cC + dD at constant temperature, the equilibrium constant Kc = [C]^c[D]^d / ([A]^a[B]^b relates equilibrium concentrations.

concepts.name: Writing Equilibrium Constant Expressions
concepts.explanation: Procedure to construct Kc by placing product concentrations in the numerator and reactants in the denominator, each raised to their stoichiometric coefficients from the balanced equation.

concepts.name: Temperature Dependence of Kc
concepts.explanation: Temperature is the only factor that changes the value of Kc; raising T favors the endothermic direction, lowering T favors the exothermic direction, altering product-to-reactant ratios at equilibrium.

concepts.name: Pressure Effect on Gaseous Equilibria
concepts.explanation: For all-gas systems with unequal moles on each side, increasing pressure shifts equilibrium toward the side with fewer gas molecules; no effect if moles of gas are equal on both sides.

concepts.name: Catalyst Effect on Equilibrium
concepts.explanation: A catalyst increases the rate of both forward and reverse reactions equally, reducing time to reach equilibrium but not changing the equilibrium position or Kc.

concepts.name: Closed System Requirement for Equilibrium
concepts.explanation: A sealed system where matter cannot enter or leave is needed for establishing and maintaining chemical equilibrium in reactions, especially with gases.

concepts.name: Equilibrium Calculations with Kc (ICE Method)
concepts.explanation: A structured approach using Initial, Change, and Equilibrium amounts to solve for unknown concentrations at equilibrium by substituting into the Kc expression.

concepts.name: Units and Stoichiometric Dependence of Kc
concepts.explanation: Kc units depend on net concentration exponents; reversing or scaling the balanced equation inverts or roots K accordingly, so the associated equation must be stated with Kc.

concepts.name: Reversible Reaction Notation (⇌)
concepts.explanation: Use of the equilibrium arrow to denote reversible reactions in which products can reform reactants.

concepts.name: Demonstration: NO2/N2O4 Temperature Equilibrium
concepts.explanation: An experiment showing color changes (brown NO2 to colorless N2O4) with temperature shifts, visualizing Le Chatelier's Principle for an exothermic dimerization.

concepts.name: Demonstration: Fe3+ + SCN− ⇌ Fe(SCN)2+ Equilibrium
concepts.explanation: A colorimetric equilibrium (yellow/colorless to red complex) used to probe Le Chatelier shifts due to concentration and temperature changes.

concepts.name: Haber–Bosch Process Optimization via Le Chatelier
concepts.explanation: Industrial application optimizing ammonia yield using high pressure (fewer moles on product side), moderate temperature (exothermic reaction vs rate), and iron catalyst with recycle/removal strategies.

concepts.name: Ionic Product of Water (Kw)
concepts.explanation: Kw = [H+][OH−] quantifies water’s self-ionization; increases with temperature because the process is endothermic.

concepts.name: Self-Ionisation of Water
concepts.explanation: The equilibrium H2O ⇌ H+ + OH− (or 2H2O ⇌ H3O+ + OH−) that generates equal concentrations of H+ and OH− in pure water.

concepts.name: pH Definition and Calculation
concepts.explanation: pH = −log10[H+] provides a logarithmic measure of acidity; used to quantify acidic, basic, or neutral solutions.

concepts.name: pH–pOH Relationship at 25°C
concepts.explanation: For dilute aqueous solutions at 25°C, pH + pOH = 14, linking hydrogen and hydroxide ion concentrations via Kw.

concepts.name: Calculating pH of Strong Acids and Bases
concepts.explanation: Assuming full dissociation, [H+] or [OH−] equals the formal concentration (adjusting for stoichiometry), enabling direct pH or pOH computation.

concepts.name: Acid Dissociation Constant (Ka) and Base Dissociation Constant (Kb)
concepts.explanation: Equilibrium constants defining the extent of acid or base dissociation in water; larger Ka or Kb indicates a stronger acid or base.

concepts.name: Relative Strengths of Conjugate Acid–Base Pairs
concepts.explanation: Strong acids have weak conjugate bases and weak acids have strong conjugate bases, reflecting position of acid–base equilibria.

concepts.name: Distinguishing Strong vs. Concentrated
concepts.explanation: ‘Strong’ refers to dissociation extent (Ka/Kb), not concentration; a dilute strong acid can have higher pH than a concentrated weak acid.

concepts.name: Approximate pH of Weak Acids and Bases
concepts.explanation: Using the square-root approximation for weak electrolytes: [H+] ≈ √(Ka·M_acid) and [OH−] ≈ √(Kb·M_base) when dissociation is small.

concepts.name: Acid–Base Indicators as Weak Acids/Bases
concepts.explanation: Indicators are weak acids/bases whose acid and conjugate forms have different colors; added H+ or OH− shifts the indicator equilibrium (Le Chatelier), changing color.

concepts.name: Indicator pH Range and Selection
concepts.explanation: Each indicator has a characteristic pH interval over which it changes color; choose an indicator whose range lies within the steep vertical region of the titration curve.

concepts.name: Universal Indicator
concepts.explanation: A mixture of indicators providing a broad, continuous color change across pH 1–14 for approximate pH estimation.

concepts.name: pH Titration Curves for Strong/Weak Acid–Base Pairs
concepts.explanation: Characteristic pH vs volume profiles for strong–strong (sharp jump near pH 7), strong acid–weak base (jump below 7), weak acid–strong base (jump above 7), and weak–weak (no sharp jump).

concepts.name: pH Sensors vs Indicators
concepts.explanation: pH electrodes provide precise numerical pH independent of solution color, reducing subjectivity compared to color indicators.

concepts.name: Calibration of pH Sensors with Buffer Solutions
concepts.explanation: Adjusting a pH probe’s response to known buffer pH values (e.g., pH 3 and 10) to ensure accurate and precise measurements; proper storage prevents drift.

concepts.name: Buffer Solution (Definition and Role in Calibration)
concepts.explanation: A solution that resists pH change upon small additions of acid or base; used as stable standards for pH sensor calibration.

concepts.name: Limitations of the pH Scale
concepts.explanation: Practical pH range is ~0–14 for dilute aqueous solutions; values outside occur but strong non-idealities arise above 1 M and in nonaqueous media.

concepts.name: Conductivity to Distinguish Strong and Weak Electrolytes
concepts.explanation: At equal concentrations, strong acids/bases show much higher conductivity than weak ones due to greater ionization.

concepts.name: Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) test
concepts.explanation: A measure of dissolved oxygen consumed by microbial activity when a water sample is kept at 20°C in the dark for five days; calculated from the difference between initial and day-5 dissolved O2 readings.

concepts.name: Eutrophication
concepts.explanation: Nutrient enrichment (notably NO3− and PO43−) of water leading to excessive algal growth, increased microbial decomposition, oxygen depletion, and fish kills.

concepts.name: Chlorination and hypochlorous acid formation
concepts.explanation: Disinfection step where chlorine reacts with water to form hypochlorous acid (HOCl), the primary antimicrobial species: Cl2 + H2O → HOCl + HCl.

concepts.name: Flocculation in water treatment
concepts.explanation: Coagulation of fine suspended particles into removable flocs using flocculants such as Al2(SO4)3 to aid subsequent sedimentation/filtration.

concepts.name: Sand filtration
concepts.explanation: Physical removal of remaining suspended solids by percolating water through graded sand layers where particulates are trapped between grains.

concepts.name: Sedimentation (settling) in water treatment
concepts.explanation: Gravity-driven settling of suspended solids and flocs in large tanks to produce clarified overflow and sludge underflow.

concepts.name: Ultraviolet (UV) disinfection of water
concepts.explanation: Exposure of water to germicidal UV wavelengths to inactivate microorganisms without chemical addition; effectiveness depends on turbidity and lamp maintenance.

concepts.name: Fluoridation of drinking water
concepts.explanation: Addition of fluoride compounds (e.g., NaF, H2SiF6) at ~1 ppm to reduce tooth decay by strengthening enamel; excess leads to fluorosis.

concepts.name: pH adjustment in water treatment
concepts.explanation: Control of distribution-system corrosion and water quality by raising pH with Ca(OH)2 or lowering with H2SO4/CO2 and managing hardness/softening effects.

concepts.name: Microfiltration membranes
concepts.explanation: Pressure-driven membrane filtration using polymeric pores (~0.1–10 µm) to remove suspended solids and bacteria (not viruses) from water.

concepts.name: Microplastics in aquatic systems
concepts.explanation: Plastic particles <5 mm (primary or secondary) that persist, transport toxins, are ingested by organisms, and can pass through treatment barriers into water supplies.

concepts.name: Acidification of freshwater bodies
concepts.explanation: pH lowering by acid rain or acidic discharges, increasing metal ion release (e.g., Al3+), damaging biota via enzyme disruption and shell dissolution.

concepts.name: Ocean acidification and carbonate chemistry
concepts.explanation: Dissolution of CO2 forming carbonic acid (CO2 + H2O → H2CO3) that shifts carbonate equilibria, dissolving CaCO3 shells: CaCO3 + H2CO3 → Ca2+ + 2 HCO3−.

concepts.name: Solubility of gases in water versus temperature
concepts.explanation: Gas solubility decreases with increasing temperature, reducing dissolved O2 levels critical for aquatic life (e.g., ~11.3 mg/L at 10°C vs ~9.2 mg/L at 20°C).

concepts.name: Natural greenhouse effect
concepts.explanation: Atmospheric gases (e.g., CO2, H2O, CH4, N2O) absorb Earth’s outgoing IR and re-radiate it, maintaining a life-supporting average surface temperature.

concepts.name: Global Warming Potential (GWP)
concepts.explanation: A metric comparing heat trapping by a greenhouse gas to CO2 over a fixed time (e.g., 100 years), incorporating radiative efficiency and atmospheric lifetime.

concepts.name: Residence time of atmospheric carbon dioxide
concepts.explanation: Average time CO2 remains in the atmosphere (~100 years), limited by slow ocean mixing and carbon sink uptake relative to emission rates.

concepts.name: NOx formation and indirect greenhouse effect
concepts.explanation: High-temperature combustion forms NO that oxidizes to NO2; NOx promotes tropospheric ozone formation, an additional greenhouse gas.

concepts.name: Sulfur oxides and aerosol cooling
concepts.explanation: SO2/SO3 from combustion or volcanism form sulfuric acid aerosols that reflect sunlight, exerting a net cooling rather than greenhouse warming.

concepts.name: Deionised versus distilled water
concepts.explanation: Distilled water is free of dissolved/suspended solids and gases; deionised water lacks ions but can contain dissolved gases and non-ionic organics.

concepts.name: Water softening by sodium carbonate
concepts.explanation: Addition of Na2CO3 precipitates Ca2+/Mg2+ as carbonates, reducing hardness; may raise pH and affect taste.

concepts.name: Chlorine residual in treated water
concepts.explanation: A controlled low concentration of free chlorine maintained in distribution to ensure ongoing disinfection and protection against recontamination.

concepts.name: Carbon capture and storage (CCS)
concepts.explanation: Industrial process capturing CO2 from flue gases, compressing, transporting, and injecting it into geological formations to prevent atmospheric release.

concepts.name: Thermochemistry
concepts.explanation: The study of heat changes associated with chemical reactions and physical processes, typically at constant pressure.

concepts.name: Enthalpy change (ΔH) at constant pressure
concepts.explanation: The overall energy exchanged with the surroundings when a chemical reaction or physical change occurs at constant pressure; negative for exothermic, positive for endothermic processes.

concepts.name: Thermochemical equation
concepts.explanation: A balanced chemical equation that includes physical states and the enthalpy change per mole of reaction under stated conditions; ΔH scales with stoichiometry.

concepts.name: Exothermic reaction
concepts.explanation: A chemical reaction that releases heat to the surroundings; products have lower enthalpy than reactants and ΔH is negative.

concepts.name: Endothermic reaction
concepts.explanation: A chemical reaction that absorbs heat from the surroundings; products have higher enthalpy than reactants and ΔH is positive.

concepts.name: Enthalpy profile diagram
concepts.explanation: A diagram that shows the relative enthalpies of reactants and products to illustrate exothermic or endothermic changes, distinct from activation energy–focused reaction profiles.

concepts.name: Heat of combustion (ΔH_comb)
concepts.explanation: The heat change when one mole of a substance is completely burned in excess oxygen; typically measured in kJ mol−1 and negative.

concepts.name: Calorimetry with spirit burners (heat of combustion of alcohols)
concepts.explanation: An experimental procedure using a spirit burner and a copper calorimeter to heat a known mass of water; uses q = mcΔT and fuel mass loss to estimate ΔH_comb.

concepts.name: Specific heat capacity (c)
concepts.explanation: The amount of heat required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1 K; used in calorimetry (q = mcΔT).

concepts.name: Bomb calorimeter
concepts.explanation: An instrument for accurate measurement of heats of combustion in a sealed vessel; enables precise calorimetry of fuels.

concepts.name: Bond enthalpy (average bond dissociation energy)
concepts.explanation: The average energy required to break one mole of a specified covalent bond in the gas phase to separated neutral atoms; bond breaking is endothermic and formation is exothermic.

concepts.name: Estimating reaction enthalpy from bond enthalpies
concepts.explanation: Approximating ΔH for a reaction by ΔH ≈ ΣE(bonds broken) − ΣE(bonds formed), using tabulated average bond enthalpies.

concepts.name: Enthalpy of neutralisation (ΔH_neut)
concepts.explanation: The heat change when one mole of H+ from an acid reacts with one mole of OH− from a base to form water; ~−57 kJ mol−1 for strong acid–strong base, smaller magnitude for weak acids/bases.

concepts.name: Polystyrene-cup calorimetry for neutralisation
concepts.explanation: A constant-pressure calorimetry method mixing acid and base in an insulated cup, measuring ΔT to compute ΔH using mass, c, and temperature rise; assumes solution density ~1 g cm−3.

concepts.name: Standard enthalpy of formation (ΔH_f°)
concepts.explanation: The enthalpy change when one mole of a compound in its standard state is formed from its elements in their standard states; elements in standard states have ΔH_f° = 0; formation equations may use fractional coefficients.

concepts.name: Hess's Law
concepts.explanation: The enthalpy change for a reaction is independent of the pathway; enthalpy changes for multi-step processes add to the same total as the one-step reaction; enables calculation of unknown ΔH by combining equations.

concepts.name: Standard conditions for enthalpy measurements
concepts.explanation: Tabulated enthalpy changes are measured at 25 °C (298 K) and 1 atm (1.01325×10^5 Pa), ensuring comparability across data sources.

concepts.name: Thermal decomposition
concepts.explanation: A reaction in which heat breaks a compound into simpler substances; typically endothermic (e.g., CaCO3 → CaO + CO2).

concepts.name: Enthalpy of fusion (ΔH_fus)
concepts.explanation: Energy absorbed when one mole of a solid melts to a liquid at constant pressure; e.g., ice has ΔH_fus = +6.01 kJ mol−1.

concepts.name: Enthalpy of vaporisation (ΔH_vap)
concepts.explanation: Energy absorbed when one mole of a liquid vaporises to a gas at constant pressure; larger than fusion due to full separation of particles; released upon condensation.

concepts.name: Enthalpy of solution (ΔH_sol)
concepts.explanation: The enthalpy change when one mole of a solute dissolves in water to form an infinitely dilute solution at 25 °C and 1 atm; can be endothermic or exothermic.

concepts.name: Complete vs incomplete combustion of hydrocarbons
concepts.explanation: Complete combustion forms only CO2 and H2O with sufficient O2; oxygen limitation leads to incomplete combustion producing CO and/or carbon (soot).

concepts.name: Trends in heats of combustion across homologous series
concepts.explanation: For alkanes and primary alcohols, ΔH_comb becomes more exothermic roughly linearly with each added CH2 unit; alcohols have lower ΔH_comb than corresponding alkanes due to pre-existing oxygen; alkenes/alkynes are lower than alkanes due to fewer H atoms (less H2O formed) and stronger multiple bonds that require more energy to break.

concepts.name: System and surroundings in thermochemistry
concepts.explanation: The chemical system comprises reactants and products; the surroundings are everything else; heat flow sign conventions refer to energy exchange between system and surroundings.

concepts.name: Enthalpy (H)
concepts.explanation: The total heat content (state function) stored in a chemical system; absolute H cannot be measured directly, only changes (ΔH).

concepts.name: Galvanic (Voltaic) Cell Operation
concepts.explanation: A device that converts chemical energy to electrical energy via coupled oxidation and reduction reactions occurring in two half-cells connected by a salt bridge; electrons flow from the anode to the cathode (e.g., Zn/Cu cell ~1.1 V).

concepts.name: Electrochemical Series and Standard Electrode Potentials (E°)
concepts.explanation: A ranked list of elements by their standard electrode potentials measured versus the standard hydrogen electrode, used to predict ease of oxidation/reduction, displacement reactions, and cell voltages under standard conditions.

concepts.name: Standard Hydrogen Electrode (SHE)
concepts.explanation: The reference half-cell (Pt electrode in 1 M H+, H2 gas at 1 atm) assigned E° = 0.00 V, used to determine standard electrode potentials of other half-cells.

concepts.name: Lithium‑Ion Battery: Structure and Intercalation Mechanism
concepts.explanation: Rechargeable cell comprising a graphite anode hosting intercalated Li+, a LiCoO2 cathode, an organic electrolyte, and a separator; Li+ reversibly intercalates/deintercalates between electrodes while electrons travel through the external circuit.

concepts.name: Lithium‑Ion Cell Discharge Reactions and Ion/Electron Flows
concepts.explanation: During discharge: anode oxidation LiC6 → Li+ + e− + C6; cathode reduction Li+ + e− + CoO2 → LiCoO2; overall LiC6 + CoO2 → C6 + LiCoO2; electrons flow in the external circuit, Li+ through the electrolyte/separator.

concepts.name: Lithium‑Ion Cell Charging Reactions (Electrolytic Operation)
concepts.explanation: An external power source reverses the discharge reactions: at the positive electrode LiCoO2 → Li+ + e− + CoO2; at the negative electrode Li+ + e− + C6 → LiC6; electrode roles (signs) are reversed relative to discharge.

concepts.name: Electrolytic Cell: Definition and Comparison with Galvanic Cell
concepts.explanation: A system where electrical energy drives a non‑spontaneous chemical change; contrasts with galvanic cells where spontaneous redox produces electricity; electrode sign conventions are reversed, though cathode is still reduction and anode oxidation.

concepts.name: Hydrogen‑Oxygen Proton Exchange Membrane (PEM) Fuel Cell Operation
concepts.explanation: H2 is oxidized at a Pt/C anode to H+ and e−; H+ crosses a hydrated proton exchange membrane while e− go through the external circuit; O2 is reduced at the cathode to form H2O; continuous reactant feed enables steady electricity generation.

concepts.name: Electrode (Anode/Cathode) Definitions and Roles in Galvanic Cells
concepts.explanation: In galvanic cells the anode is the negative electrode where oxidation occurs and electrons are released; the cathode is the positive electrode where reduction occurs and electrons are accepted.

concepts.name: Electrode Sign Conventions in Electrolysis
concepts.explanation: In electrolytic cells, the cathode is negative (site of reduction) and the anode is positive (site of oxidation) because an external power source drives electrons onto the cathode.

concepts.name: CROA Principle (Cathode Reduction, Oxidation Anode)
concepts.explanation: A mnemonic stating that reduction always occurs at the cathode and oxidation at the anode, applicable to both galvanic and electrolytic cells.

concepts.name: Electrolyte: Definition and Function
concepts.explanation: A molten, solution, or gel phase containing mobile ions that conducts electricity by ion migration while typically blocking electron flow; provides ionic pathways in cells.

concepts.name: Salt Bridge Function in Galvanic Cells
concepts.explanation: An ionic conduit (e.g., KCl/KNO3-soaked medium) connecting two half‑cells to maintain electroneutrality by ion migration without bulk mixing, preventing charge buildup and sustaining current.

concepts.name: Half‑Cell Concept
concepts.explanation: A portion of an electrochemical cell consisting of an electrode and its ion-containing solution where either oxidation or reduction occurs; two half‑cells make a full cell.

concepts.name: Primary Cells (Non‑rechargeable)
concepts.explanation: Galvanic cells designed for single use with irreversible chemistry (e.g., zinc‑carbon, alkaline, some lithium); typical cell voltage ~1.5 V.

concepts.name: Secondary Cells (Rechargeable)
concepts.explanation: Cells with reversible chemistry that can be recharged multiple times (e.g., lithium‑ion ~3.8 V per cell, lead‑acid 2 V per cell).

concepts.name: Metal Displacement Reactions from Solutions
concepts.explanation: A metal higher in the electrochemical series displaces a lower metal from its salt solution, reflecting relative tendencies to oxidize and enabling predictions of reaction feasibility.

concepts.name: Corrosion of Metals and Rusting of Iron
concepts.explanation: Undesired oxidation of metals to compounds; rusting of iron (formation of hydrated iron(III) oxide) requires both oxygen and water; passivating oxides (e.g., Al2O3) can inhibit further corrosion.

concepts.name: Cathodic Protection via Sacrificial Anodes
concepts.explanation: Corrosion prevention by electrically coupling iron/steel to a more active metal (e.g., Zn) that oxidizes preferentially, keeping the protected metal as the cathode.

concepts.name: Galvanizing (Zinc Coating) for Corrosion Protection
concepts.explanation: Applying a zinc layer to steel/iron provides barrier protection and sacrificial oxidation, as zinc is higher in the electrochemical series and corrodes preferentially.

concepts.name: Electrolysis of Acidified Water (Hofmann Voltameter)
concepts.explanation: Using dilute H2SO4 and inert electrodes to split water: cathode 2H+ + 2e− → H2; anode H2O → 2H+ + 1/2 O2 + 2e−; gases collected in a 2:1 H2:O2 volume ratio.

concepts.name: Electrolysis of Copper(II) Chloride Solution
concepts.explanation: With inert electrodes, Cu2+ is reduced at the cathode to copper metal and Cl− is oxidized at the anode to chlorine gas: Cu2+ + 2e− → Cu; 2Cl− → Cl2 + 2e−.

concepts.name: Electrolysis of Potassium Iodide Solution with Phenolphthalein
concepts.explanation: At the anode: 2I− → I2 + 2e− (brown iodine); at the cathode: 2H2O + 2e− → H2 + 2OH− (solution turns pink with phenolphthalein), demonstrating competing discharge of water.

concepts.name: Inert Electrodes in Electrolysis (Graphite and Platinum)
concepts.explanation: Chemically unreactive electrodes, commonly graphite or platinum, that serve to conduct electrons into/out of the electrolyte without participating in the reaction.

concepts.name: Cell versus Battery Distinction
concepts.explanation: A cell is a single electrochemical unit; a battery consists of two or more cells connected together (often in series) to increase voltage or capacity.

concepts.name: Quantum Mechanical Model of the Atom
concepts.explanation: Modern atomic model where electrons occupy orbitals defined by wavefunctions and quantized quantum numbers, predicting electron distributions and chemical behavior.

concepts.name: Bohr Model of the Atom
concepts.explanation: Atom model with electrons in fixed circular orbits and quantized energy levels explaining line spectra, especially of hydrogen.

concepts.name: Rutherford Nuclear Model of the Atom
concepts.explanation: Model proposing a dense, positively charged nucleus with electrons occupying the surrounding space, replacing the plum pudding model.

concepts.name: Electron Configuration
concepts.explanation: The ordered filling of electrons into energy levels, sublevels, and orbitals to represent the ground-state arrangement of electrons in atoms.

concepts.name: Atomic Orbitals
concepts.explanation: Regions of space (s, p, d, f) with specific shapes and energies where electrons have high probability of being found.

concepts.name: Energy Sublevels (s, p, d, f)
concepts.explanation: Subdivisions of principal energy levels with distinct energies and capacities that determine electron distribution.

concepts.name: Atomic Number and Mass Number
concepts.explanation: Atomic number (Z) is the number of protons; mass number (A) is the total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.

concepts.name: Isotopes
concepts.explanation: Atoms of the same element with the same atomic number but different mass numbers due to differing numbers of neutrons.

concepts.name: Relative Atomic Mass (Ar)
concepts.explanation: The weighted average mass of an element’s isotopes relative to 1/12 of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.

concepts.name: Properties of Subatomic Particles
concepts.explanation: Charges, relative masses, and locations of protons, neutrons, and electrons that determine atomic identity and behavior.

concepts.name: Periodic Trend: Ionization Energy
concepts.explanation: The energy required to remove an electron from a gaseous atom; trends increase across a period and decrease down a group.

concepts.name: Electronegativity
concepts.explanation: A measure of an atom’s ability to attract shared electrons in a bond; trends increase across periods and decrease down groups.

concepts.name: Periodic Trend: Atomic Radius
concepts.explanation: A measure of atomic size that decreases across a period and increases down a group due to effective nuclear charge and shielding.

concepts.name: Hund's Rule
concepts.explanation: Electrons occupy degenerate orbitals singly with parallel spins before pairing, minimizing electron repulsion.

concepts.name: Electron Configuration of Ions
concepts.explanation: Writing electron arrangements for cations and anions, including the removal of electrons from highest energy orbitals first (e.g., 4s before 3d for transition metals).

concepts.name: Rutherford Scattering Experiment
concepts.explanation: Gold foil alpha-scattering experiment that provided evidence for a small, dense, positively charged nucleus.

concepts.name: Atomic Emission Spectra
concepts.explanation: Discrete spectral lines emitted by excited atoms as electrons transition between quantized energy levels, evidence for quantization.

concepts.name: Limitations of the Rutherford Model
concepts.explanation: Rutherford’s model could not explain atomic stability or discrete line spectra, necessitating quantized energy levels.

concepts.name: Limitations of the Bohr Model
concepts.explanation: Bohr’s model works mainly for hydrogen-like species and fails for multi-electron atoms and fine spectral details, prompting orbital theory.

concepts.name: Plum Pudding Model
concepts.explanation: Thomson’s pre-nuclear model with electrons embedded in a diffuse positive charge, later disproven by scattering experiments.

concepts.name: Discovery of the Proton
concepts.explanation: Identification of the positively charged nuclear particle, establishing atomic number as proton count.

concepts.name: Discovery of the Neutron
concepts.explanation: Identification of the neutral nuclear particle explaining isotopes and accounting for nuclear mass.

concepts.name: Law of Conservation of Mass
concepts.explanation: In a chemical reaction, mass is neither created nor destroyed; total mass of reactants equals total mass of products.

concepts.name: Balancing Chemical Equations
concepts.explanation: Adjusting coefficients so atoms of each element are conserved on both sides of a chemical equation.

concepts.name: Mole Concept in Stoichiometry
concepts.explanation: Using moles and molar ratios from balanced equations to relate amounts of reactants and products.

concepts.name: Percentage Composition by Mass
concepts.explanation: Calculating the mass percent of each element in a compound from its formula or analytical data.

concepts.name: Empirical Formula from Percent Composition
concepts.explanation: Determining the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms from mass percentage data.

concepts.name: Empirical Formula from Masses of Reactants and Products
concepts.explanation: Deriving empirical formulas using conservation of mass and measured masses consumed/produced in reactions.

concepts.name: Mass–Mass Stoichiometry Calculations
concepts.explanation: Computing masses of reactants or products using molar masses and mole ratios from balanced equations.

concepts.name: Gas Volume Stoichiometry
concepts.explanation: Using molar volume relationships of gases to calculate volumes in reactions under specified conditions.

concepts.name: Limiting Reactant
concepts.explanation: Identifying the reactant that is consumed first and limits the extent of reaction and product yield.

concepts.name: Percentage Yield
concepts.explanation: Comparing actual product obtained to theoretical yield to assess reaction efficiency.

concepts.name: Arrhenius Theory of Acids and Bases
concepts.explanation: Defines acids as producers of H+ in water and bases as producers of OH− in water.

concepts.name: Brønsted–Lowry Acid–Base Theory
concepts.explanation: Defines acids as proton donors and bases as proton acceptors; applies beyond aqueous solutions.

concepts.name: Conjugate Acid–Base Pairs
concepts.explanation: Pairs of species that differ by one proton; acid-base reactions viewed as proton-transfer equilibria.

concepts.name: Neutralisation Reactions
concepts.explanation: Acid and base react to form water and a salt; often exothermic.

concepts.name: Acid–Carbonate Reactions
concepts.explanation: Acids react with carbonates/hydrogencarbonates to produce salt, water, and carbon dioxide gas.

concepts.name: Acid–Metal Reactions
concepts.explanation: Reactive metals with acids produce a salt and hydrogen gas.

concepts.name: Solution Concentration: Percentage
concepts.explanation: Expressing concentration as percent by mass, volume, or mass/volume depending on context.

concepts.name: Parts Per Million (ppm)
concepts.explanation: A concentration unit denoting parts of solute per million parts of solution or mixture.

concepts.name: Molarity (mol L⁻¹)
concepts.explanation: Concentration defined as moles of solute per litre of solution.

concepts.name: Dilution Calculations
concepts.explanation: Using C1V1 = C2V2 to compute volumes or concentrations when preparing diluted solutions.

concepts.name: Standard Solution Preparation
concepts.explanation: Making a solution of accurately known concentration using a primary standard and volumetric glassware.

concepts.name: Acid–Base Titration Technique
concepts.explanation: Procedure using a burette, pipette, and indicator (or pH meter) to determine unknown concentration via neutralisation.

concepts.name: Calculating Concentration from Titration Data
concepts.explanation: Using balanced equations, titration volumes, and molarity to find unknown concentrations.

concepts.name: Accuracy and Precision in Volumetric Analysis
concepts.explanation: Understanding random and systematic errors, significant figures, and proper technique to improve titration data quality.

concepts.name: Oxidation and Reduction as Electron Transfer
concepts.explanation: Redox defined by loss (oxidation) and gain (reduction) of electrons; occurs concurrently.

concepts.name: Oxidation Numbers
concepts.explanation: Bookkeeping tool assigning charges to atoms to track electron transfer in reactions.

concepts.name: Balancing Redox Equations (Half-Equation Method)
concepts.explanation: Separating oxidation and reduction, balancing mass and charge, then combining to obtain the overall balanced redox reaction.

concepts.name: Permanganate–Iron(II) Titration
concepts.explanation: Redox titration where MnO4− oxidises Fe2+ to Fe3+; MnO4− acts as self-indicator.

concepts.name: Iodine–Thiosulfate Titration
concepts.explanation: Iodometric method where I2 is titrated with thiosulfate; starch used as endpoint indicator.

concepts.name: Reaction Rate and Its Measurement
concepts.explanation: Rate as change in concentration per unit time; measured via gas volume, mass loss, colorimetry, or conductivity.

concepts.name: Factors Affecting Reaction Rate
concepts.explanation: Temperature, concentration, surface area, and catalysts influence collision frequency and energy distribution.

concepts.name: Collision Theory
concepts.explanation: Reactions occur when particles collide with sufficient energy and proper orientation.

concepts.name: Activation Energy
concepts.explanation: Minimum energy required for reacting species to form the activated complex and proceed to products.

concepts.name: Dynamic Chemical Equilibrium
concepts.explanation: State where forward and reverse reaction rates are equal and concentrations remain constant.

concepts.name: Le Chatelier’s Principle
concepts.explanation: A system at equilibrium shifts to oppose changes in concentration, temperature, or pressure.

concepts.name: Equilibrium Constant (Kc)
concepts.explanation: Ratio of product concentrations to reactant concentrations at equilibrium, each raised to stoichiometric coefficients.

concepts.name: Law of Chemical Equilibrium Calculations
concepts.explanation: Using equilibrium expressions and ICE tables to compute unknown concentrations and extents of reaction.

concepts.name: Autoionisation of Water and Kw
concepts.explanation: Water self-ionises to H3O+ and OH−; the ionic product Kw governs pH relationships.

concepts.name: pH Scale
concepts.explanation: Logarithmic measure of acidity/alkalinity defined as pH = −log10[H+].

concepts.name: Acid and Base Strength
concepts.explanation: Extent of ionisation or proton donation/acceptance; strong vs weak acids and bases.

concepts.name: pH of Strong Acids and Bases
concepts.explanation: Calculating pH from complete dissociation assumptions of strong monoprotic acids and strong bases.

concepts.name: pH of Weak Acids and Bases
concepts.explanation: Using Ka or Kb and equilibrium approximations to compute pH of weak electrolytes and their solutions.

concepts.name: Acid–Base Indicators
concepts.explanation: Weak acids/bases with distinct color changes over specific pH ranges used to detect titration endpoints.

concepts.name: Enthalpy Change (ΔH)
concepts.explanation: Heat exchanged at constant pressure for a process; sign indicates endothermic or exothermic.

concepts.name: Heat of Combustion
concepts.explanation: Enthalpy change when one mole of a substance burns completely in oxygen.

concepts.name: Bond Enthalpy
concepts.explanation: Average energy required to break one mole of a bond in gaseous molecules; used to estimate reaction enthalpies.

concepts.name: Enthalpy of Neutralisation
concepts.explanation: Enthalpy change when an acid and base react to form one mole of water under standard conditions.

concepts.name: Standard Enthalpy of Formation
concepts.explanation: Enthalpy change when one mole of a compound forms from its elements in their standard states.

concepts.name: Hess’s Law
concepts.explanation: Total enthalpy change of a reaction is path-independent; sum of steps equals overall ΔH.

concepts.name: Galvanic (Voltaic) Cells
concepts.explanation: Electrochemical cells that convert chemical energy to electrical energy via spontaneous redox reactions.

concepts.name: Electrochemical Series
concepts.explanation: Arranged reduction potentials predicting direction of redox reactions and relative oxidising/reducing strengths.

concepts.name: Primary and Secondary Cells
concepts.explanation: Comparison of non-rechargeable (primary) and rechargeable (secondary) batteries in terms of chemistry and use.

concepts.name: Fuel Cells
concepts.explanation: Electrochemical devices generating electricity from continuous reactant supply, with high efficiency and low emissions.

concepts.name: Electrolytic Cells
concepts.explanation: Use of electrical energy to drive non-spontaneous chemical reactions such as electrolysis.

concepts.name: Water Treatment Processes
concepts.explanation: Stages such as screening, coagulation, filtration, and disinfection to make water potable.

concepts.name: Carbon Cycle
concepts.explanation: Biogeochemical cycling of carbon between atmosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere, and geosphere.

concepts.name: Natural and Enhanced Greenhouse Effect
concepts.explanation: Greenhouse gases trap infrared radiation; anthropogenic increases enhance warming beyond natural levels.

concepts.name: Greenhouse Gases and Greenhouse Factors
concepts.explanation: Roles of CO2, CH4, N2O, etc., and their relative warming potentials in atmospheric heating.

concepts.name: Allotropes of Carbon
concepts.explanation: Different structural forms of carbon such as diamond, graphite, and fullerenes with distinct properties.

concepts.name: Alkanes
concepts.explanation: Saturated hydrocarbons with single C–C bonds; general formula CnH2n+2 and typical substitution reactions.

concepts.name: Alkenes
concepts.explanation: Unsaturated hydrocarbons containing C=C double bonds; undergo addition reactions and show geometric isomerism.

concepts.name: Cis–Trans (Geometric) Isomerism
concepts.explanation: Stereoisomerism due to restricted rotation around double bonds leading to different spatial arrangements.

concepts.name: Alkynes
concepts.explanation: Unsaturated hydrocarbons with C≡C triple bonds, more reactive in addition reactions than alkenes.

concepts.name: Aromatic Hydrocarbons
concepts.explanation: Compounds containing benzene rings with delocalised π electrons exhibiting substitution reactivity.

concepts.name: Chloroalkanes
concepts.explanation: Alkane derivatives with one or more chlorine atoms; undergo nucleophilic substitution.

concepts.name: Alcohols
concepts.explanation: Organic compounds with hydroxyl groups; show hydrogen bonding and undergo oxidation and substitution reactions.

concepts.name: Aldehydes
concepts.explanation: Carbonyl compounds with formyl group; readily oxidised and used in qualitative tests (e.g., Fehling’s, Tollens’).

concepts.name: Ketones
concepts.explanation: Carbonyl compounds with internal C=O; less easily oxidised than aldehydes and show characteristic reactivity.

concepts.name: Carboxylic Acids
concepts.explanation: Organic acids with –COOH group; weak acids that form salts and esters and show hydrogen bonding.

concepts.name: Esters
concepts.explanation: Derived from carboxylic acids and alcohols; formed by esterification, often fragrant, and hydrolysed to parent compounds.

concepts.name: Structural Isomerism
concepts.explanation: Compounds with the same molecular formula but different connectivity, leading to different properties.

concepts.name: Substitution Reactions (Organic)
concepts.explanation: Reaction where an atom or group in a molecule is replaced by another, typical of alkanes and aromatics.

concepts.name: Addition Reactions (Organic)
concepts.explanation: Atoms or groups add across multiple bonds, characteristic of alkenes and alkynes.

concepts.name: Elimination Reactions (Organic)
concepts.explanation: Removal of atoms/groups from adjacent carbons forming multiple bonds, often the reverse of addition.

concepts.name: Organic Redox Reactions
concepts.explanation: Oxidation and reduction processes involving changes in C–H and C–O bonding, e.g., alcohol to aldehyde/ketone.

concepts.name: Acid–Base Reactions of Organic Compounds
concepts.explanation: Acidity/basicity of functional groups (e.g., carboxylic acids, amines) and their proton-transfer reactions.

concepts.name: Scientific Method
concepts.explanation: A step-by-step process for investigating questions in chemistry: observation, question, hypothesis, experiment, data collection, analysis, conclusion, and repetition to validate results.

concepts.name: Hypothesis (If–Then Statement)
concepts.explanation: A testable, evidence-based prediction written as an if–then statement that explains a proposed cause–effect relationship.

concepts.name: Scientific Theory
concepts.explanation: An evidence-based explanation of observations built from hypotheses, laws, and facts; may change with new evidence.

concepts.name: Scientific Law
concepts.explanation: A concise description of consistent natural phenomena without explaining why they occur.

concepts.name: Models in Chemistry
concepts.explanation: Simplified representations that bridge macroscopic observations and microscopic entities to explain and predict chemical behavior.

concepts.name: Particle Model of Matter
concepts.explanation: Matter is composed of small particles whose motion and arrangement explain macroscopic properties like boiling and gas behavior.

concepts.name: Dalton's Atomic Model
concepts.explanation: An early atomic model treating atoms as indivisible solid spheres; later revised after discovery of subatomic particles.

concepts.name: Subatomic Particles in the Atom
concepts.explanation: Atoms contain smaller particles (electrons, protons, neutrons), leading to modern atomic models beyond Dalton’s.

concepts.name: Quantitative Data in Chemistry
concepts.explanation: Numerical measurements such as mass, volume, temperature, and time collected using instruments.

concepts.name: Qualitative Data in Chemistry
concepts.explanation: Descriptive observations like color change, precipitate formation, or gas evolution during experiments.

concepts.name: Repeatability
concepts.explanation: Getting the same results when the same person repeats an experiment using the same method and conditions.

concepts.name: Reproducibility
concepts.explanation: Independent researchers in different laboratories obtain the same results by following the same method.

concepts.name: Reliability of Data
concepts.explanation: The consistency of measurements across repeated trials, indicating dependable results for valid conclusions.

concepts.name: IUPAC Nomenclature Standards
concepts.explanation: International rules for naming elements and compounds to ensure consistent chemical communication.

concepts.name: SI Units in Chemistry
concepts.explanation: Use of the International System of Units (e.g., meter, kilogram, second) for standardized chemical measurements.

concepts.name: Gas Pressure–Volume Relationship (Particle Model)
concepts.explanation: Decreasing a gas’s volume increases its pressure due to more frequent particle collisions in a smaller space.

concepts.name: Effect of Concentration on Reaction Rate
concepts.explanation: Increasing reactant concentration generally increases the rate of reaction, as observed in acid–carbonate systems.

concepts.name: Measuring Reaction Rate via CO2 Evolution
concepts.explanation: Determining reaction rate by measuring mass or volume of CO2 produced over time in acid–carbonate reactions.

concepts.name: Peer Review in Scientific Publishing
concepts.explanation: Independent expert evaluation of research methods and conclusions prior to publication to ensure validity.

concepts.name: Ball-and-Stick Molecular Models (Molymod)
concepts.explanation: Physical models using balls and connectors to represent atoms and bonds for visualizing molecular shapes and bonding.

concepts.name: Rutherford gold foil scattering experiment
concepts.explanation: Bombardment of thin gold foil with alpha particles showed most pass through, some deflect at large angles, and a few rebound, leading to the nuclear model.

concepts.name: Updated nuclear model with neutrons
concepts.explanation: Refinement of the nuclear model incorporating neutrons with protons in the nucleus, explaining nuclear mass and improved stability.

concepts.name: Properties of subatomic particles (relative charge and mass)
concepts.explanation: Proton: charge +1, mass 1; Neutron: charge 0, mass 1; Electron: charge −1, mass 1/1838; locations: protons and neutrons in nucleus, electrons outside.

concepts.name: Discovery of the electron
concepts.explanation: Thomson showed cathode rays are streams of negatively charged particles (electrons), establishing the first subatomic particle.

concepts.name: Thomson e/m measurement for the electron
concepts.explanation: Determination of the electron’s charge-to-mass ratio by deflecting a narrow cathode ray beam between charged plates and measuring displacement.

concepts.name: Millikan oil drop experiment
concepts.explanation: Measured the elementary charge (−1.6×10^-19 C) by balancing gravitational and electric forces on charged oil droplets, enabling calculation of electron mass with Thomson’s e/m.

concepts.name: Plum pudding model of the atom
concepts.explanation: Thomson’s pre-nuclear model: a sphere of diffuse positive charge with electrons embedded randomly; later disproven by scattering data.

concepts.name: Discovery of the proton via alpha bombardment
concepts.explanation: Rutherford observed emission of small positively charged particles from light elements when bombarded with alpha particles, naming them protons.

concepts.name: Discovery of the neutron (Chadwick)
concepts.explanation: Alpha particles striking beryllium produced neutral particles that ejected protons from paraffin wax; identified as neutrons with mass ≈ proton.

concepts.name: Particulate nature of matter
concepts.explanation: All substances consist of tiny particles (atoms, molecules, or ions), providing a basis for explaining macroscopic properties and behavior.

concepts.name: Ammonia–hydrogen chloride diffusion experiment
concepts.explanation: Gases diffusing from opposite ends of a tube form a white ring of ammonium chloride where they meet, evidencing particle motion and diffusion.

concepts.name: Cathode rays
concepts.explanation: Streams of electrons emitted from the cathode in discharge tubes; invisible but cause fluorescence and cast shadows, deflected by electric fields.

concepts.name: Crookes discharge tube experiment
concepts.explanation: Passing electricity through low-pressure gas revealed rays from the cathode that produced fluorescence and shadows (Maltese cross), evidencing cathode rays.

concepts.name: Alpha particles (helium nuclei)
concepts.explanation: Positively charged particles consisting of two protons and two neutrons; used as probes in scattering experiments.

concepts.name: Electron cloud concept
concepts.explanation: Electrons occupy the space around the nucleus rather than residing in the nucleus, accounting for the atom’s size and mostly empty space.

concepts.name: Limitations of Rutherford's nuclear model
concepts.explanation: Could not explain why protons in the nucleus do not repel apart and why electrons do not lose energy and spiral into the nucleus.

concepts.name: Relative size of nucleus versus atom
concepts.explanation: The nuclear diameter is about 1/100,000 of the atomic diameter, explaining why most alpha particles pass through foil undeflected.

concepts.name: Role of neutrons in nuclear stability
concepts.explanation: Neutrons help stabilize the nucleus by mitigating proton–proton electrostatic repulsion, preventing the nucleus from flying apart.

concepts.name: Quantised Energy Levels in Atoms
concepts.explanation: Electrons in atoms can possess only specific, fixed energy values (energy levels), not a continuum.

concepts.name: Bohr Model of the Atom (Assumptions)
concepts.explanation: Electrons revolve in fixed orbits (energy levels) around the nucleus; each orbit has quantised energy labeled by n.

concepts.name: Emission Line Spectrum
concepts.explanation: A spectrum of discrete coloured lines produced when excited atoms emit light at specific frequencies corresponding to electronic transitions.

concepts.name: Planck Relation for Atomic Transitions (E2 - E1 = h f)
concepts.explanation: The frequency of emitted or absorbed light equals the energy difference between two levels divided by Planck’s constant.

concepts.name: Ground State and Excited State of Atoms
concepts.explanation: Ground state has electrons in lowest available energy levels; excited states have electrons promoted to higher levels after energy absorption.

concepts.name: Spectroscopic Evidence for Energy Levels
concepts.explanation: Discrete spectral lines and their calculable wavelengths confirm that electrons occupy fixed energy levels in atoms.

concepts.name: Orbital Model (Quantum Mechanical Model) of the Atom
concepts.explanation: Electrons are described by probability distributions (orbitals) derived from wave mechanics rather than fixed paths.

concepts.name: Atomic Orbitals (Probability Definition)
concepts.explanation: A three-dimensional region in space with high probability (about 95%) of finding an electron.

concepts.name: s Orbital Shape
concepts.explanation: s orbitals are spherical probability distributions that increase in size with increasing principal quantum number.

concepts.name: p Orbital Shapes and Orientation
concepts.explanation: p orbitals are dumbbell-shaped; three degenerate orbitals (px, py, pz) oriented along orthogonal axes.

concepts.name: Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle (Atomic Context)
concepts.explanation: It is impossible to know simultaneously the exact position and velocity of an electron, supporting a probabilistic electron model.

concepts.name: de Broglie Wave-Particle Duality of Electrons
concepts.explanation: Electrons exhibit wave-like behavior with detectable wavelengths, undermining fixed classical orbits.

concepts.name: Hydrogen Discharge Tube Experiment
concepts.explanation: Low-pressure hydrogen excited by an electric current emits a line spectrum, foundational evidence for quantized levels.

concepts.name: Hydrogen Spectral Series: Lyman
concepts.explanation: Ultraviolet lines produced by electron transitions terminating at n = 1 in hydrogen.

concepts.name: Hydrogen Spectral Series: Balmer
concepts.explanation: Visible lines produced by electron transitions terminating at n = 2 in hydrogen.

concepts.name: Hydrogen Spectral Series: Paschen
concepts.explanation: Infrared lines produced by electron transitions terminating at n = 3 in hydrogen.

concepts.name: Relationship between Electron Transitions and Spectral Line Color
concepts.explanation: The color (frequency) of an emission line is determined by the energy gap between initial and final levels; some colors are absent if no matching transition exists.

concepts.name: Element Identification by Emission Spectra
concepts.explanation: Each element has a unique line emission spectrum that can be used as a fingerprint for qualitative identification.

concepts.name: Flame Test Procedure for Metal Ions
concepts.explanation: Using a damp splint or platinum wire to introduce metal salts into a Bunsen flame to observe characteristic colors (e.g., Na yellow, K lilac, Cu blue-green).

concepts.name: Spectrometer vs Spectroscope
concepts.explanation: A spectrometer measures spectral properties (e.g., wavelength), whereas a spectroscope is used for observation only.

concepts.name: Splitting of Spectral Lines (Fine Structure)
concepts.explanation: Single spectral lines often resolve into closely spaced lines, evidencing sublevels (e.g., sodium yellow doublet).

concepts.name: Photon (Definition in Atomic Transitions)
concepts.explanation: A discrete packet of electromagnetic energy emitted or absorbed when an electron changes energy levels.

concepts.name: Continuous Spectrum
concepts.explanation: An unbroken spread of colors (e.g., white light through a prism) with no gaps between wavelengths.

concepts.name: Electron configuration using sublevels (s, p, d)
concepts.explanation: Represents electron arrangements by filling s, p, and d sublevels in order of increasing energy (e.g., 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 4s2 3d6).

concepts.name: Aufbau principle
concepts.explanation: Electrons fill the lowest available energy sublevels first when building the ground-state electron configuration.

concepts.name: Hund's Rule of Maximum Multiplicity
concepts.explanation: Electrons occupy orbitals of equal energy singly with parallel spins before pairing, maximizing the number of unpaired electrons.

concepts.name: Pauli Exclusion Principle
concepts.explanation: No more than two electrons may occupy a single orbital, and paired electrons must have opposite spins.

concepts.name: Sublevel filling order: 4s before 3d
concepts.explanation: Because the 4s sublevel lies slightly lower in energy than 3d in neutral atoms, electrons fill 4s prior to 3d.

concepts.name: Electron configuration exceptions: chromium and copper
concepts.explanation: Cr and Cu exhibit anomalous configurations (Cr: [Ar] 4s1 3d5; Cu: [Ar] 4s1 3d10) due to extra stability of half-filled and filled sublevels.

concepts.name: Electron configurations of ions and isoelectronic species
concepts.explanation: Ions form by loss or gain of electrons; cations lose electrons (often from 4s before 3d), anions gain; different species may share identical electron configurations.

concepts.name: Electron configuration (Bohr model shells)
concepts.explanation: Lists electrons by principal energy levels (e.g., K = 2,8,8,1), useful for the first 20–36 elements.

concepts.name: 2n^2 rule for shell capacity
concepts.explanation: The maximum number of electrons in a principal energy level n is 2n^2 (e.g., n=1 holds 2, n=2 holds 8, n=3 holds 18).

concepts.name: Modern Periodic Law
concepts.explanation: When elements are arranged by increasing atomic number, their properties recur periodically.

concepts.name: Atomic number (Z)
concepts.explanation: Number of protons in an atom’s nucleus; defines the element and its position in the modern Periodic Table.

concepts.name: Mass number (A)
concepts.explanation: Sum of protons and neutrons in an atom’s nucleus; always a whole number.

concepts.name: Nuclear notation (A/Z X) and neutron calculation
concepts.explanation: Represents an element with mass number A and atomic number Z; neutrons = A − Z.

concepts.name: Mass spectrometer for isotope analysis
concepts.explanation: Instrument that measures isotope masses and abundances to determine Ar and identify compounds.

concepts.name: Mendeleev's Periodic Law
concepts.explanation: Arrangement by increasing atomic weight led to periodic recurrence of properties and grouping of similar elements.

concepts.name: Mendeleev's predictions and eka-elements
concepts.explanation: Left gaps and correctly predicted properties of undiscovered elements (e.g., eka-silicon → germanium, eka-aluminium → gallium).

concepts.name: Moseley’s X-ray determination of atomic number
concepts.explanation: Showed X-ray frequency correlates with nuclear charge, establishing atomic number as the correct basis for ordering elements.

concepts.name: Modern vs Mendeleev periodic tables
concepts.explanation: Modern table orders by atomic number, has no gaps, and separates the d-block; Mendeleev used atomic weight and left gaps.

concepts.name: Transition elements (d-block) placement
concepts.explanation: In the modern Periodic Table, the transition metals occupy a central d-block distinct from s- and p-block elements.

concepts.name: Definition of an element (Boyle)
concepts.explanation: A substance that cannot be split into simpler substances by chemical means.

concepts.name: Electrolysis to isolate elements (Davy)
concepts.explanation: Discovery that passing electricity through compounds can liberate elemental metals (e.g., K, Na, Ca).

concepts.name: Octet Rule
concepts.explanation: Atoms tend to achieve an arrangement with eight electrons in their outermost energy level during bonding; a guiding principle with notable exceptions (e.g., H, He, transition metals).

concepts.name: Ionic Bonding
concepts.explanation: Electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions formed by complete transfer of electrons from one atom to another.

concepts.name: Covalent Bonding
concepts.explanation: Chemical bond formed when two atoms share one or more pairs of electrons, producing discrete molecules.

concepts.name: Lewis Dot-and-Cross Diagrams
concepts.explanation: Representation of valence electrons as dots and crosses around element symbols to model ionic and covalent bonding and electron transfer/sharing.

concepts.name: VSEPR Theory
concepts.explanation: Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion theory: electron pairs around a central atom repel and arrange to minimize repulsion, determining molecular shape and approximate bond angles.

concepts.name: Sigma Bond (σ bond)
concepts.explanation: Covalent bond formed by head-on (axial) overlap of orbitals; stronger and formed first in multiple bonds; can involve s, p, or d orbitals.

concepts.name: Pi Bond (π bond)
concepts.explanation: Covalent bond formed by sideways overlap of p (or d) orbitals; weaker than sigma bonds and occurs alongside a sigma bond in double and triple bonds.

concepts.name: Multiple Covalent Bonds
concepts.explanation: Double bonds involve two shared electron pairs (one σ and one π); triple bonds involve three pairs (one σ and two π), enabling octet completion and affecting bond strength/length.

concepts.name: Lone Pairs and Bond Pairs
concepts.explanation: Non-bonding electron pairs (lone pairs) and bonding pairs influence molecular geometry; lone pairs exert greater repulsion, compressing bond angles (e.g., NH3 107°, H2O 104.5°).

concepts.name: Writing Formulas of Ionic Compounds
concepts.explanation: Formulas are determined by balancing total positive and negative charges to neutrality, using ion charges (including Roman numerals for variable-valency metals).

concepts.name: Polyatomic Ions (Common Charges)
concepts.explanation: Charged groups of atoms (e.g., sulfate SO4^2−, nitrate NO3^−, carbonate CO3^2−, hydroxide OH^−, ammonium NH4^+) with fixed formulas and charges used in ionic compounds.

concepts.name: Transition Metals: Variable Valency
concepts.explanation: Many transition metals form ions with different positive charges due to small energy gaps between 4s and 3d sublevels, leading to variable oxidation states (e.g., Fe2+, Fe3+).

concepts.name: Transition Metal (Definition)
concepts.explanation: An element that forms at least one ion with a partially filled d sublevel; excludes Sc3+ (empty d) and Zn2+ (full d).

concepts.name: Ionic Crystal Lattice (NaCl Structure)
concepts.explanation: Regular 3D arrangement of ions in a crystal; NaCl has a cubic unit cell with each Na+ coordinated by 6 Cl− and vice versa, repeating to form a lattice.

concepts.name: Valency (Classical Definition)
concepts.explanation: Combining power of an element defined by the number of hydrogen atoms (or other monovalent atoms) it bonds with (e.g., H 1, O 2, N 3, C 4).

concepts.name: Cations and Anions
concepts.explanation: Positively charged ions (cations) formed by electron loss and negatively charged ions (anions) formed by electron gain; may be monatomic or polyatomic.

concepts.name: Precipitation Reaction
concepts.explanation: Reaction in solution that forms an insoluble solid (precipitate), e.g., Ag+ + Cl− → AgCl(s).

concepts.name: Aqueous Solution
concepts.explanation: A solution where water is the solvent; denoted as aqueous and essential medium for many ionic tests.

concepts.name: Qualitative Analysis
concepts.explanation: Analytical approach focused on detecting the presence of specific ions or compounds rather than their quantity.

concepts.name: Chloride Ion Test (AgNO3 with Ammonia Confirmation)
concepts.explanation: Add AgNO3 to a chloride solution to form white AgCl precipitate; confirm by dissolution in dilute ammonia.

concepts.name: Sulfate vs. Sulfite Test (BaCl2 and Dilute HCl)
concepts.explanation: Add BaCl2 to form white precipitate; BaSO4 remains insoluble in dilute HCl (sulfate), BaSO3 dissolves due to SO2 formation (sulfite).

concepts.name: Carbonate/Hydrogencarbonate Test with Acid and Limewater
concepts.explanation: Add dilute acid to release CO2, which turns limewater milky via CaCO3 formation; applies to CO3^2− and HCO3^−.

concepts.name: Distinguishing Carbonate vs. Hydrogencarbonate (MgSO4 Test)
concepts.explanation: MgSO4 forms a white MgCO3 precipitate with carbonate but no precipitate with hydrogencarbonate unless boiled (then MgCO3 forms).

concepts.name: Limewater Test for Carbon Dioxide
concepts.explanation: CO2 bubbled through Ca(OH)2 produces milky CaCO3; excess CO2 clears milkiness by forming soluble Ca(HCO3)2.

concepts.name: Brown Ring Test for Nitrate Ion
concepts.explanation: Layer concentrated H2SO4 under a mixture of nitrate solution and freshly prepared FeSO4; formation of a brown ring at the interface confirms NO3−.

concepts.name: Phosphate Ion Test (Ammonium Molybdate and Nitric Acid)
concepts.explanation: Add (NH4)2MoO4 and concentrated HNO3 to a phosphate solution, then warm; formation of a yellow precipitate (ammonium phosphomolybdate) confirms PO4^3−.

concepts.name: Polar covalent bond
concepts.explanation: A covalent bond with unequal sharing of electrons, producing partial charges (δ+ and δ−) on the bonded atoms.

concepts.name: Pure covalent bond
concepts.explanation: A covalent bond with equal sharing of electrons, typically between atoms of identical or very similar electronegativity.

concepts.name: Polar molecule
concepts.explanation: A molecule with an uneven distribution of charge, having separated centers of partial positive and partial negative charge.

concepts.name: Non-polar molecule
concepts.explanation: A molecule with an even distribution of charge where the centers of partial positive and negative charges coincide, often due to molecular symmetry.

concepts.name: Molecular shape and polarity
concepts.explanation: Molecular geometry can cause polar bonds to add or cancel; asymmetric shapes yield polar molecules, symmetric shapes can render molecules non-polar.

concepts.name: Electronegativity-difference rule-of-thumb
